news.head: ETF outflows
news.text: Spot ETH ETFs had net outflows in all five weeks ending in October, about −$1.65B for the month, the largest monthly outflow since they launched (previous record −$1.42B, Nov 2025). Oct 30 alone: −$155.85M. Total net assets fell from $17.60B to $13.22B during October.

news.head: Large holders
news.text: Lookonchain reported one wallet spent $62.97M over five hours to buy 27,553 ETH at about $2,286, after earlier buying 16,658 ETH with 37.96M USDC. Earlier in the week (Oct 29 report) the biggest holders sold about 160,000 ETH.

news.head: THORChain halt
news.text: A one-block Ethereum reorg on Oct 31 (11:34 UTC) dropped a deposit THORChain had already credited; its solvency checker halted ETH swaps and node operators then halted ten chains as a precaution. THORChain says it was not an Ethereum protocol hack; the user returned the funds.

news.head: Binance hack
news.text: About $6.3B was stolen from Binance on Oct 29. On Nov 1 Binance restored withdrawals for BTC; ETH, USDT and USDC on Ethereum; BNB, USDT and USDC on BSC; XRP; and ETH and USDC on Base, with more to return in phases. It says it has covered about 95% of the affected amount from its own funds; about $3B is frozen.
news.source: CoinDesk, Nov 1; Binance on X via CoinGabbar, Nov 2

news.head: The Fed
news.text: The Fed held rates at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28 in a 10–2 vote. Reported odds of a December hike range from 75% to 84% depending on the source.

news.head: Glamsterdam upgrade
news.text: Ethereum developers postponed Glamsterdam's Hoodi testnet activation on Oct 22. No mainnet date is set.

news.head: Staking
news.text: Staking inflows reached 7.96M ETH in the first nine months of 2026, a record amount of ETH committed to staking.

rules.text: Each week, Seats vote how the fund's book is split across a fixed list of tokens. Gains are measured in ETH; WETH is the cash sleeve.
No more than 25% of the book in any one token. WETH has no cap.
The fund never sells its own $TMF. Only the rest of the book is split.
A token gets nothing that week unless cards holding at least half the weight cast give it something. Otherwise its share stays in WETH.
The dials only change if at least 25 different Seats vote. Otherwise last week's settings stay.
Profit take: 0–50% of the week's confirmed gain paid out in kind. Expense ratio: 0–20% of the fund's fee income burned.
Each Friday the fund moves at most a fifth of the book toward the voted split, and only as much as each pool can take while moving its price about half a percent.
Dividends are paid on the lower of two readings at least six days apart, using 30-minute average prices.
Only Seats enrolled before the week began. One card per Seat per week; once counted it can't be changed.
Voting closes Friday 20:00 UTC: 3pm New York in winter, 4pm in summer. The chain's clock ignores daylight saving.

glossary.def: ETH in token form. The fund's cash sleeve: holding it means no gain and no loss against ETH.
Global Dollar, a dollar stablecoin issued by Paxos.
The fund's own token. The fund never sells it, and it isn't part of the split.
One vote in a fund. Each Seat casts one card per week.
A Seat's vote: a % for each token plus the two dials.
The share of a week's confirmed gain paid out as dividends, in kind (0–50%).
The share of the fund's fee income that gets burned (0–20%).
A token only gets money if cards holding at least half the vote weight give it something.
The ballot's label for a token that doesn't have enough backing yet.
The ballot's estimate of how many Fridays the fund needs to build a token up to 25% of the fund, given how much its pool can take.
The token's price in WETH on Robinhood Chain, as shown on the ballot.
The weekly close, Friday 20:00 UTC. Cards are counted then.
All the cards cast so far in a fund this week, added together. The ballot shows what the room would do if the bell rang now.
A ballot template that fills a card with the room's current split. This dashboard reads each fund's room from that view.
No card in that fund gives the token anything so far, so the ballot doesn't list it as vetoed or backed.
A fund's timeline for the week: one point per ballot capture, showing seats, what the room backs and $TMF held.
Monthly survey indexes of US manufacturing and services activity from the Institute for Supply Management. Above 50 means activity grew that month.
Money put into a fund's shares minus money taken out on a given day. Negative means more was taken out than put in.
Seats signed up to vote in a fund this week. Only Seats enrolled before the week began can cast a card.
Seats that have voted this week out of the fund's enrolled Seats, read from the Ballot and DividendOffice contracts on Robinhood Chain.

The room worked out from every card returned on Robinhood Chain this week: a token is backed when seats holding more than half the voting weight put something on it, and its share is the seat-weighted average of all cards. $TMF held comes from the fund's own books. Checked against ballot captures; it can differ from the ballot page by a few tenths of a point.
When a blockchain replaces its most recent block(s) with a different version, so transactions in the dropped block may not count.
